facts.heading: GP suggested visit due to exhaustion

facts.evidence: My general practitioner suggested I come. She said I look exhausted

facts.heading: Burnout started in October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burnt out since October.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burnt out since October

facts.heading: Workload increased after client loss

facts.evidence: We lost a big client, half of the team got moved onto the rescue plan

facts.heading: Daniel doing three people's jobs

facts.evidence: so I ended up doing three people's jobs

facts.heading: Working late into the night

facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by 7 and I'm still answering messages at 10 that night

facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about 4 hours

facts.heading: Wakes up at 3 am

facts.evidence: I wake up at 3 in the morning and just can't fall back asleep

facts.heading: Father diagnosed with Parkinson's

facts.evidence: my father. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn

facts.heading: Hannah lives in Toronto

facts.evidence: My angry sister Hannah lives in Toronto

facts.heading: Daniel feels guilty about care

facts.evidence: Guilty for even saying it

facts.evidence: She asks how I am and I say fine

facts.heading: Daniel avoids hospital visits

facts.evidence: some days I sit in a car park at a hospital for 10 minutes before I go in

facts.heading: GP attributed issues to stress
facts.content: Daniel's GP stated that his exhaustion was due to stress.
facts.evidence: She said it's stress and exhaustion

facts.heading: Girlfriend Claire booked session
facts.content: Daniel's girlfriend, Claire, booked the session.
facts.evidence: A girlfriend booked her, to be honest. Claire

facts.heading: Claire is worried about Daniel
facts.content: Claire is worried about Daniel, as she noticed he was disappearing.
facts.evidence: She said she was done watching me disappear

facts.heading: Daniel avoids weekend trips
facts.content: Daniel has consistently said no to his girlfriend's suggestion of going away for the weekend.
facts.evidence: I always said no

facts.heading: Work emails prevent rest
facts.content: Daniel feels that if he takes time off, he will return to 200 emails.
facts.evidence: I'll come back to 200 of them

facts.heading: Daniel stopped running recently

facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago. My legs feel like lead

facts.heading: Boss sends late emails

facts.evidence: he sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast

facts.heading: Daniel answers all boss's emails
facts.content: Daniel answers every email sent by his boss, even when he is not feeling well.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm not bad

facts.heading: Fear of job loss due to restructuring
facts.content: Daniel is worried about being let go due to a restructuring happening this spring.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring this spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Financial responsibility
facts.content: Daniel has a mortgage.
facts.evidence: I have a mortgage.

facts.heading: Reported physical symptoms
facts.content: Daniel reports feeling flat and irritable.
facts.evidence: Flat, mostly. And irritable.

facts.heading: Panic attack symptoms experienced
facts.content: Daniel experienced heart racing and shaking hands in the toilets.
facts.evidence: My heart was going and my hands were shaking.

facts.heading: Past panic attack on train
facts.content: Daniel experienced a similar episode on a train to Manchester.
facts.evidence: Once on a train to Manchester, just to get off and stand on a platform.

facts.heading: Fear of losing control
facts.content: Daniel fears that the symptoms mean he is losing his mind or coping.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. That I'm going to end up, like, I don't know, coping.

facts.heading: Substance use for coping
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee daily and has started having wine in the evenings.
facts.evidence: Coffee, probably. I want about six cups a day. And I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off.

facts.heading: Wine use duration
facts.content: Daniel drinks two to three glasses of wine in the evenings.
facts.evidence: Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Sleeplessness pattern
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at three in the morning.
facts.evidence: I wake at three anyway.

facts.heading: Relief from sharing burdens
facts.content: Daniel felt a sense of relief after sharing his burdens.
facts.evidence: A bit of relief actually. Like putting it on bad, but I didn't realize I was carrying.

facts.heading: Primary need is sleep
facts.content: Daniel believes that if he could sleep, he could cope with other issues.
facts.evidence: The nights, I think. If I could sleep, I could probably cope with the rest.

facts.heading: Family influence on coping
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather worked at the mines in Yorkshire and never complained.
facts.evidence: My grandfather worked at the mines in Yorkshire. He never complained about anything.

facts.heading: Belief about grandfather's view
facts.content: Daniel fears his grandfather would view him as weak for being in therapy.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here.

facts.heading: Agreed to try small change
facts.content: Daniel agreed to try setting a fixed time in the evening to switch off his phone.
facts.evidence: Yeah, half past nine perhaps.

facts.heading: Plan for tracking sleep
facts.content: Daniel will write down how his night goes when he wakes up.
facts.evidence: I can do that. Right down when I wake up. If I wake up.
